newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise as liquidity dries up, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise as liquidity dries up, seen up.

text.p: Russian shares rose on pre-holiday buying on Tuesday afternoon after a morning dip, and traders predicted the market would continue to move upwards, despite light volumes, ahead of the long weekend.
"I think we'll close higher today, I don't think there will be a very big rise," said Ilya Galtsov, a trader at Trinfiko.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index had risen to 303.92 at 1200 GMT after closing on Monday at 301.54.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2365 at 1350 GMT from $0.2305 at the close on Monday. Regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.284 from $1.265.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS edged up to $0.715 from $0.701 while international long-distance telecom Rostelekom RTKM.RTS sat tight at $3.53.

UES announced on Tuesday consolidated 1996 pre-tax profits of 11 trillion roubles calculated according to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis and a five-rouble dividend on ordinary and preferred shares, unchanged from 1995.
Dealers said a number of second tier shares, especially small regional telecoms, were doing well on encouraging 1996 financial results released recently.

But traders said Russian and domestic investors were building up positions in the liquidity-driven market ahead of holidays May 1-4 and 9-11 when shares will be harder to find. Many expect a general market pickup towards the end of May.
"Everyone is buying before the holidays hoping the market will rise further," said CentreInvest Securities trader Sergei Bukin. "It is speculative."
